findings.title: Existing admin permission clients are not upgraded with the new Clients resource type and scopes
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null, so realms that already had the admin permissions client created under the previous V2 schema will not get the newly added Clients resource type or its scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). Later, client permission creation can fail with ModelException "No scopes found." and client permission evaluation can fail or NPE because the all-Clients resource is missing. The init method needs to be idempotent and add missing schema entries for existing admin permission clients.

findings.title: Per-client permission check can dereference a null all-clients resource
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) may return null when the all-resource for the Clients type does not exist. The code then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, causing a NullPointerException. This is especially likely for an existing admin permissions client that was not upgraded with the new schema. The method should handle resource == null by returning false or ensuring initialization first.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic all-clients resource name
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type CLIENTS, including the all-clients resource whose name is AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients"). If a policy grants the requested scope on that all-resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and the code adds resource.getName(), i.e. "Clients", to the returned set. Callers expect this set to contain concrete client IDs, so the all-resource grant is not expanded into actual clients and a nonexistent client ID is returned. The all-resource should be skipped or expanded to the corresponding concrete client IDs.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName has special handling for the USERS resource type but not for the newly added CLIENTS resource type. For client permissions/resources it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources created by getOrCreateResource use the client's internal id as the resource name and do not set a meaningful display name. Resource name resolution or representation output for client permissions can therefore be null or an internal UUID instead of the client's clientId. A CLIENTS branch should resolve the client and return client.getClientId() or another appropriate display value.

findings.title: Void require methods are documented as returning boolean
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true if ... returns true", but both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding check fails. This misdocuments the API and should say that it throws ForbiddenException when the check returns false.
